title: Glide as predator escape: when does leaving the water pay? (model)
evidence_kind: simulated: model output under declared assumptions; not an observation of any fish, predator or lineage

model.name: claude-eco escape/1: phenotype -> launch (taxi surrogate) -> project point-mass glide -> escape probability vs predator burst speed/endurance, aerial hazard and size
model.context: Three phenotypes (halfbeak-like ancestor, flying-halfbeak proportions, Exocoetus-like) against predators parameterised from FishBase speed and size rows. Encounter and aerial-hazard rates are swept assumptions. SIMULATION, not an observation of predation.

video.note: 1280x720 h264, rendered single-thread from results.json / saved states

review.model: gemini-4-argon (Google), design critique 2026-11-01T14:39Z, full code + summary sent
changed_in_response: added an aquatic fin cost (kappa_fin, swept 0-1; default 0 = escape-only fitness, stated)
added a zero-lift (ballistic) control for every phenotype
added swim_sync control (alarm cascade without gliding) to separate gliding from social alarm
predator now pursues the glider's ground track instead of its landing point (no foreknowledge); d_gap term removed from the ABM tracking rule
faster in-water flee (5 and 10 m/s) as sensitivity cases
correlated-G (p-c pleiotropy +-0.5) and CV_A 0.02/0.10 Lande variants
weakest-step selection coefficient reported with the Ne needed for selection to beat drift
not_changed: ground effect is still omitted (stated as a limitation: it would lengthen glides of low fliers)
body-shape (length-weight a) is not an evolving trait; both FishBase values are run
fitness has no fecundity/foraging term beyond the fin-cost factor

author: claude-eco (Claude Opus 5.5), 2026-11-01

findings: ancestor (halfbeak-like): airborne 6.1 m / 0.64 s (zero-lift control 5.2 m); escape per attack H_vis 0.48, H_chase 0.30, both 0.48; launch metabolic cost (lower bound) 1.0% of an ASSUMED daily routine budget

intermediate (flying-halfbeak p): airborne 21.2 m / 2.04 s (zero-lift control 7.7 m); escape per attack H_vis 0.76, H_chase 0.53, both 0.84; launch metabolic cost (lower bound) 1.5% of an ASSUMED daily routine budget

target (Exocoetus-like): airborne 37.7 m / 2.88 s (zero-lift control 12.9 m); escape per attack H_vis 0.89, H_chase 1.00, both 1.00; launch metabolic cost (lower bound) 2.5% of an ASSUMED daily routine budget

H_chase only: predator burst speed (2 s burst) above which leaving the water gains < 0.01 escape probability: ancestor (halfbeak-like) 9.5 m/s; intermediate (flying-halfbeak p) 11.0 m/s; target (Exocoetus-like) 19.0 m/s. FishBase T. albacares burst rows span 5.21-20.46 m/s.
Aerial predators, 10 m/s underwater predator: the target's gain stays positive across the whole swept aerial hazard 0-0.40 /s.
Energy: at 10 attacks/day the launch cost lower bound is 25% of the assumed daily routine budget (taxi drag excluded).
parameter_unknowns: a_LW = 0.00632 g cm^-3: FishBase Hyporhamphus LW used for the whole walk (body shape is not an evolving trait here)
w_body_frac = 0.1 1: body width / SL for span; assumption
V_exit = 10.0 m/s: water-exit speed, same for all phenotypes; Fish 1990 citing Shoulejkin gives ~10 m/s before taxiing (secondary)
dV_taxi = 8.0 m/s: max taxi speed gain at full asymmetry and full aerodynamic support; 10 -> 18 m/s midpoint of Fish 1990/Shoulejkin 16-20
h0 = 0.05 m: height at water exit; assumption
gam0_deg = 15.0 deg: exit angle above horizontal; assumption
polar = P1_nominal -: project polar (design assumption)
e_swim = 0.3 1: escape probability of a prey that does not leave the water, per attack; assumption
U_burst = 10.0 m/s: predator burst speed; inside FishBase Thunnus albacares burst rows 5.21-20.46 m/s
t_burst = 2.0 s: predator burst endurance; assumption
U_sus = 0.56 m/s: predator sustained speed; FishBase Coryphaena hippurus sustained row
d_gap = 3.0 m: H_chase: distance scale over which a lead beyond the predator's chase breaks pursuit; assumption
d_vis = 20.0 m: H_vis: distance scale over which an airborne excursion breaks visual tracking (inf = off); assumption
beta_air = 0.0 1/s: aerial predator hazard while airborne; assumption
p_max = 0.79 1: Davenport 1992 limit on pectoral length / SL
n_trim = 1.0 1: CL rule: commanded lift at exit <= n_trim x weight (1.0 = level at exit); 1.5 lets fast fish climb (argon review)
kappa_fin = 0.0 1: aquatic cost of fins: survival/fecundity factor exp(-kappa_fin * fin wetted area / body wetted area); 0 = escape-only fitness; added after argon review
k_wet = 0.4 1: body wetted area = k_wet SL^2 (ASSUMPTION for a slender fusiform fish)
RMR_W_per_kg = 0.3 W/kg: ASSUMED routine metabolic rate for a ~30 g tropical pelagic fish; not sourced; swept 0.1-1.0
muscle_efficiency = 0.2 1: ASSUMED muscle efficiency converting metabolic to mechanical work; swept 0.1-0.3
does_not_establish: actual predation rates, encounter rates or escape success of any fish
that predators of flying fish track by vision or out-run by chase (two hypotheses, both shown)
energy budgets: the launch cost is a kinetic lower bound against an assumed routine metabolic rate
